$schema-note: Hand-dispositioned. Generated by scripts/arch/secret-response-census.mjs --write, then annotated: the SCANNER supplies path/key/occurrences and the AUTHOR supplies disposition/why. `node scripts/arch/secret-response-census.mjs` fails if the scanner and this file disagree, so a new raw-secret response path cannot land without somebody writing down why it is there.
purpose: WIN-259 (M2.4) asks for the raw-secret response paths on the oracle to be
FOUND, COUNTED, NAMED, and closed where V1 can reach them. This is the
count, and the finding that matters most is the one it makes obvious:
NONE OF THE 29 IS INSIDE V1'S REACH, because V1 has no response surface
at all. apps/core-api/src/transports/* are seams — a `kind` and an
`AppModule` — and M4 owns the routes. Every occurrence below is in
apps/agent or apps/webapp, which WIN-258 T6 already put outside M2.
So the closable work was never 'delete these returns'. It was to make it
structurally impossible for M4's transports to add a twelfth site, which is
what the rest of WIN-259 does: material leaves the vault only as a value
that redacts itself, material ENTERS it only as the same (write-only
inputs), the process logger redacts what it is handed, and a refused read
now leaves evidence. This file is what M4 inherits: eleven rows it must
carry across deliberately rather than rediscover.
method: A raw-secret response path is a property whose NAME says the value is
material, in an object literal that a REQUEST HANDLER answers with. The
scanner walks the TypeScript AST, not lines, because four things a grep
cannot tell apart from a response all appear in these files: a request
body, a local variable, a JSON schema declaring an input's shape, and a
column read on the way to a store.
Three precision rules were each added because they changed the number:
* a handler frame is required — 31 occurrences became 22 once a private
OAuth config normaliser and an alert-channel normaliser stopped
* `webhookPath: webhookPathRedacted(id)` does not count — the redacted
form is the fix, and counting it would push a reader to 'close' the one
* a literal assigned to a local that the handler RETURNS does count —
without that the MCP tool table showed one reveal where it has three,
reporting the MCP surface as safer than the REST surface it mirrors.

sites.why: Create, BYO-app mint and rotate only. The secret is a segment of the inbound webhook URL the customer must paste into Slack, and it is not readable again from any endpoint. Removing the reveal makes the channel unusable rather than safer. The FILE is a legacy transport (WIN-258 T6, M4), so the shape moves with the route.

The same secret a second time, embedded in a path. It is listed separately because a reader closing `webhookSecret` alone would leave the material in the URL beside it, which is the mistake this row exists to prevent. The list endpoints already answer with webhookPathRedacted.
The same secret a third time, embedded in an absolute URL. Same reason as webhookPath: the three must be closed together or not at all.

The MCP tool table mirrors the REST controller above: channels.create, channels.mint_from_manifest and channels.rotate_webhook_secret. Two of the three are reached only through a local `const result` that is returned later, which is why the scanner needed the local-return rule to see them.
The mirror of the REST controller's webhookPath, on the same three tools. The other four tools in this file answer with webhookPathRedacted.
The mirror of the REST controller's webhookUrl, on the same three tools.

The orchestration tool's provisioning step re-serves the entity secret its own registration just minted. It is the only delivery of that secret; the entity cannot read it back, and every later read goes through the vault's runtime-tier path.

RFC 6749 section 5.1 makes access_token a REQUIRED member of the token endpoint's success response. A server that redacted it would not be an OAuth server. Four occurrences: the authorization-code and refresh-token branches of both the platform and the entity token endpoints.
RFC 6749 section 5.1 makes refresh_token an OPTIONAL member of the same response, and this server issues one. Same four branches as access_token, and closable only by dropping refresh-token support.

The create action re-serves the platform MCP bearer token the management transport just minted, once. The metadata half already passes assertCredentialSafePayload; the token half is the reveal. A Remix route is a legacy transport under WIN-258 T6, so the shape moves with M4's surface rather than here.
The same reveal for one entity's MCP token rather than the collection. Same disposition and the same owner.

indirectNote: WHAT THE SCANNER CANNOT SEE, DECLARED RATHER THAN OMITTED.
The scanner reads syntax, not types. A handler that answers with a value a
SERVICE built — `return entity`, `return result` — carries whatever that
service put in it, and no object literal at the handler names the material.
Six such paths were found by hand and are listed below. They are NOT part
of totalOccurrences, because a number that mixes a checked count with a
Each carries an `evidence` string that must still appear in its file. That
is a weaker check than the scanner's — it proves the line still exists, not
that it still reaches a response — but it is not nothing: closing the path
removes the string and this file then says so.
CLOSING THESE NEEDS TYPE INFORMATION, which means a TypeScript Program over
apps/agent rather than a per-file parse. That is a real piece of work and
it is named here rather than pretended away.

indirectSites.why: The SOURCE of the entity secret reveal. Everything below is a pass-through of this value.
The SOURCE of the entity secret ROTATION reveal, the second half of the same lifecycle.
POST /entities answers with the service value from createEntity, so the plaintextSecret rides out with no literal at the handler naming it.

POST /entities/:entityId/regenerate-secret answers with the service value from regenerateServiceSecret. Its own comment records the audit finding that made it operator-only: the serviceSecret IS the HMAC key that signs session tokens.
The MCP mirror of POST /entities. Its own description says the secret is shown once and never again, which is the behaviour, not a claim about it.
The MCP mirror of the rotate endpoint. `return result` hands back the whole service value including serviceSecret.
